quote: So we are unable to help you right now without anything built or, like, something to work off of with, like, a roof design or anything. And we don't do ground mounts here just because they are super expensive and ultimately defeat the purpose of savings.
stewart_read: This is a scenario outside Ion's standard workflow — no existing structure, a possible ground-mount ask, and a roof that doesn't exist yet. The rep handles it with a clear, honest answer rather than stringing the customer along, but this exact scenario (pre-construction lead, ground mount inquiry) isn't addressed anywhere in Ion's documented dq_rules or qualifiers — it's a genuine schema gap, not a rule the rep violated or followed.
coaching_implication: Flag for Kenny: this is a real scenario type (pre-build / land-based project) the schema doesn't yet cover. Worth confirming with Kenny whether 'no structure yet' should route to a scheduled follow-up call instead of an open-ended personal-number handoff.

quote: But, what I'll do here is I'll shoot you a text message with my personal number. So then once you have, like, a roof design built out and something like that, you can then give me a call directly, and we can help you out in getting an estimate started.
stewart_read: This isn't a bill-collection moment, but it's an analogous extension of the same anti-pattern the schema flags for bill follow-up: the rep hands out a personal number as the re-engagement mechanism instead of a tracked, company-owned follow-up path. Same privacy/scale exposure, same lack of a system record if the rep leaves or loses the thread.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may see this as the only practical option since there's no CRM-driven re-engagement flow for pre-build leads in the current script.
coaching_implication: Discuss with the manager whether there's a supported way to schedule a future callback or flag the lead for a timed follow-up instead of relying on the rep's personal number as the sole thread back to Ion.

quote: Yeah. Most definitely. And, yeah, you are right. The government incentive did go away, the, tax credit. But, nonetheless, we do have our own program here in place to completely offset it.
stewart_read: The rep runs the tax-credit rebuttal before confirming whether the customer even has a buildable project — premature program-pitch content delivered before verify/qualification is complete.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as normal opening-script sequencing (pitch line comes early in Ion's flow) rather than true scope creep, since it happens right after the interest confirmation and before verify starts.
coaching_implication: Minor — sequencing note more than a hard violation. Worth mentioning only if this rep shows a pattern of pitching before qualifying on other calls.

quote: I'm fairly certain they're now doing the selling of the power, but I'm not too certain on that.
stewart_read: Customer asks a specific, well-informed question about his utility co-op's net-metering policy (Rappahannock Electric Cooperative). The rep's answer is an audible guess rather than an admission of not knowing paired with a recovery plan — 'fairly certain... but not too certain' undercuts credibility with a customer who is clearly detail-oriented.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to use a clean knowledge-gap recovery line instead of guessing aloud — e.g., 'great question, let me get you the exact answer for your co-op rather than guess' — especially with a technically engaged customer like this one.

quote: The other thing question I have is about I I would like us I would be interested in the system that has battery banks. Yep. And is that something you could you you could help help me with?
stewart_read: Unprompted, at the very end of a call the rep was trying to close, the customer raises interest in a Tesla Powerwall battery system — a real product Ion sells. This is a second qualified interest signal the rep receives passively rather than drawing out.
coaching_implication: The rep's answer ('Of course') confirms capability but doesn't capture this as a reason to prioritize following back up with this lead once the structure is built. Coach the rep to note battery interest explicitly for whatever re-engagement record exists.

quote: Hi. Fine. Just one second. I just still got an air plug in. Okay. Corey, you said? That you were
stewart_read: Minor friction at the very top of the call — the customer is distracted (compressed air tool) and has to ask the rep to repeat his name. The rep handles it fine by re-stating clearly, but it's worth noting the intro wasn't a clean single pass.
coaching_implication: Low priority — no action needed beyond awareness; the rep recovered by simply repeating his name and company.
